title: Topical Application of Indole-3-Acetic Acid, Present in S. epidermidis Supernatant, Alleviates Atopic Dermatitis in Mice at Least via the Aryl Hydrocarbon Receptor Signalling Pathway.
authors: Wang, Piao; Wang, Caixi; Zhang, Yanting; Bi, Lingbo; Zhao, Hanqing; Xu, Zining; Wang, Ziyi; Sheng, Yujun; Cui, Yong
one_liner_zh: 该文研究吲哚-3-乙酸经AHR信号通路缓解特应性皮炎，涉及分子对接但非蛋白质-DNA互作，与本课题无关。
abstract: Dysbiosis of the skin microbiome, characterised by Staphylococcus aureus overgrowth and imbalance of commensals such as Staphylococcus epidermidis (S. epidermidis), is closely associated with atopic dermatitis (AD). However, the therapeutic relevance of defined S. epidermidis-associated indole metabolite, especially indole-3-acetic acid (IAA), in AD-like inflammation remains incompletely characterised. Here, we investigated the role of IAA, a tryptophan-derived metabolite enriched in the culture supernatant of the tested S. epidermidis strain, in AD-like inflammation. Public transcriptomic analyses suggested impaired AHR-associated and tryptophan-metabolism signatures in AD skin, particularly in lesional skin, while human metagenomic data indicated AD-associated staphylococcal alterations. Targeted metabolomics identified IAA as an enriched indole metabolite in S. epidermidis culture supernatant. In an MC903-induced AD-like mouse model, cutaneous IAA levels and S. epidermidis abundance were reduced. Topical IAA attenuated AD-like phenotypes, improved barrier-related proteins and reduced inflammatory indices. These protective effects were diminished by the AHR antagonist CH223191. Molecular docking predicted a possible interaction between IAA and AHR, and in vitro assays showed that IAA modulated keratinocyte AHR-associated inflammatory and barrier-related responses. Together, our findings support IAA as a microbiome-associated postbiotic candidate for AD management, at least partly through AHR-associated signalling.
abstract_zh: 皮肤微生物组的失调，以金黄色葡萄球菌（Staphylococcus aureus）过度生长和共生菌如表皮葡萄球菌（Staphylococcus epidermidis, S. epidermidis）失衡为特征，与特应性皮炎（atopic dermatitis, AD）密切相关。然而，特定S. epidermidis相关吲哚代谢物，尤其是吲哚-3-乙酸（indole-3-acetic acid, IAA），在AD样炎症中的治疗相关性仍未得到充分表征。在此，我们研究了IAA（一种在所测试S. epidermidis菌株培养上清液中富集的色氨酸衍生代谢物）在AD样炎症中的作用。公共转录组分析提示AD皮肤中AHR相关和色氨酸代谢特征受损，尤其是在皮损皮肤中，而人类宏基因组数据则表明AD相关的葡萄球菌改变。靶向代谢组学鉴定IAA为S. epidermidis培养上清液中富集的吲哚代谢物。在MC903诱导的AD样小鼠模型中，皮肤IAA水平和S. epidermidis丰度降低。局部应用IAA减轻了AD样表型，改善了屏障相关蛋白并降低了炎症指标。这些保护效应被AHR拮抗剂CH223191削弱。分子对接预测了IAA与AHR之间可能的相互作用，体外实验表明IAA调节角质形成细胞中AHR相关的炎症和屏障相关反应。综上所述，我们的发现支持IAA作为微生物组相关的后生元候选物用于AD管理，至少部分通过AHR相关信号通路发挥作用。
